app_store.name: OneShotLink: Secrets Once
app_store.subtitle: Self-hosted one-time links
app_store.promotional_text: Point the app at your own instance: one-time links for passwords and keys, no account needed on either end, and the reveal is one button, not a page load.
app_store.description:
OneShotLink shares a password, an API key or a note through a link that works exactly once. After the recipient opens it, the record is deleted from the server.

The difference is where it runs. You give the app the address of an instance you or your team operates. Your secrets go to your infrastructure, not to ours.

How it works:
1. Paste the secret, pick an expiry, add an optional passphrase as an extra access check.
2. Send the link. The recipient confirms before anything is consumed, so a chat preview does not spend it.
3. The secret is gone: one view, or the expiry you set.

What it does with your data, plainly: secrets are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM using a key derived from the instance secret, and deleted by an atomic compare-and-delete on reveal. The server holds that key, so it can read a secret once it is revealed. The passphrase is an access check, not a second key. This app does not claim zero-knowledge encryption, because that would not be true.

One instance, flat pricing, no seat counting. The server-side project is open source and installs with two environment variables and one compose command.
